competitions.result: Quarter-finals — lost 2–1 to West Bromwich Albion in a second replay at Maine Road, after 0–0 and 1–1 draws.
Second round — lost 3–2 at Bolton Wanderers in a replay, after a 1–1 draw at Anfield.
Third round — lost 2–0 on aggregate to Ferencváros, after eliminating Malmö and TSV 1860 Munich.

overview: Liverpool improved to third in the First Division, finishing three points behind champions Manchester City and one behind Manchester United. Their home record was strong: 17 wins from 21 matches at Anfield. Only five league victories came away from home, leaving a clear difference between their form on the two sides of the fixture list.

The summer’s principal first-team addition was Tony Hateley, bought from Chelsea for a club-record £96,000. He scored 27 goals, but Roger Hunt again finished ahead of him with 30. Hunt also became Liverpool’s overall record goalscorer in November. Emlyn Hughes was now a regular in his first full season, and Willie Stevenson moved to Stoke City in December. Ray Clemence’s £18,000 arrival from Scunthorpe strengthened the squad for the future, although Tommy Lawrence remained the first-choice goalkeeper and Clemence did not yet play a competitive first-team match.

The FA Cup required nine matches without taking Liverpool beyond the quarter-finals. Bournemouth, Walsall and Tottenham were all beaten in replays, with Hateley scoring four against Walsall. West Bromwich Albion then held Liverpool twice before winning a second replay 2–1 at Maine Road. The League Cup campaign had already ended at its first hurdle, Bolton winning the second-round replay 3–2.

There were substantial European wins, including an 8–0 defeat of TSV 1860 Munich at Anfield in the Fairs Cup. Yet Ferencváros won both legs of the next tie 1–0, ending the run in January. Liverpool finished without a trophy. Their league position and the goals from Hunt and Hateley showed that they remained competitive, while the arrival of Hughes in the regular side and Stevenson’s departure made the changes within Shankly’s team increasingly visible.

events.title: Eight goals against TSV 1860 Munich
events.detail: Liverpool won the first leg of their Fairs Cup second-round tie 8–0 at Anfield and advanced 9–2 on aggregate.

events.title: Hunt becomes Liverpool’s record scorer
events.detail: Hunt overtook Gordon Hodgson’s overall Liverpool scoring record in November 1967. Later correction of a 1966 goal attribution means sources differ over the precise match.

events.title: Ferencváros complete the European elimination
events.detail: A 1–0 defeat at Anfield followed the same score in Budapest, putting Liverpool out of the Fairs Cup in the third round.

events.title: Hateley scores four in the FA Cup
events.detail: Hateley scored four times in the 5–2 fourth-round replay win over Walsall at Anfield.

events.title: The FA Cup run ends at Maine Road
events.detail: West Bromwich Albion won the quarter-final’s second replay 2–1 after the teams had drawn at The Hawthorns and Anfield.

researchNotes: Hunt’s 30-goal total is confirmed by Liverpool FC and LFChistory: 25 league, two FA Cup and three Fairs Cup goals. Hateley’s 27 is separately confirmed by the club and specialist records.

Clemence’s £18,000 fee and June 1967 arrival are well supported, but the exact date is not: LFChistory’s transfer table gives 12 June, an LFChistory interview gives 24 June, and a Liverpool FC anniversary article implies 21 June. The entry uses summer 1967 and assigns the transfer to 1967–68.

Liverpool FC’s Hunt profile attributes the overall scoring record to the TSV Munich match on 7 November 1967; LFChistory’s corrected profile identifies Manchester United on 11 November. A 1966 goal was subsequently reclassified as a Ted Clayton own goal. Only November is published, with the disagreement preserved for review.

Departure fees for Chisnall and Wallace are omitted because published accounts disagree. Stevenson’s exact final appearance is also omitted: the official profile’s league-match wording overlooks the subsequent European appearance.

Gerry Byrne remained a significant contributor with 36 appearances. Clemence is an arrival, not a key player for a season in which he did not appear. Dave Wilson’s May 1968 return to Preston is placed in the following season as a close-season departure.
